title: Session anchoring, eviction smoothing, and scheduler queue merge
creator: Sofia Chen
description:
Motivation: Over the last 18 months we've accrued multiple, overlapping eviction heuristics and separate scheduler queues that increase tail latency during transient load spikes and complicate prefetch correctness. This ticket proposes a three-part refactor: (1) introduce "session anchoring" to keep hot conversational sessions pinned to a lightweight in-memory anchor for short timeslices to reduce repeated kvcache thrash; (2) replace the current binary eviction triggers with an eviction smoothing layer that uses exponential decay of access frequency and token-weighted cost, minimizing eviction amplification during bursts; (3) consolidate the small-per-tenant scheduler queues into a single multi-lane queue with per-session pacing heuristics and a priority bypass for interactive low-latency sessions.

Goals: Reduce 95th/99th token latency under 10% during 3x burst loads, decrease kvcache miss storm events by 60% on staging traces, simplify scheduler code path to remove three deadlock-prone synchronization points, and reduce operational complexity for rollout by enabling feature flag gates for each sub-component.

Scope & Constraints:
- Non-goal: full redesign of admission control or global batching algorithm. We are implementing localized prefetch and anchoring primitives that interoperate with the existing continuous batcher.
- Must be backwards-compatible with current KV cache on-disk layout and not require a global migration window.
- Should be feature-flagged and gradually enabled per-region.

Implementation plan (high level):
1) Session anchoring layer (libanchor): lightweight in-memory anchor table keyed by session_id; anchors store a small hotset of KV keys, a last-access timestamp, and a short lease token. Anchors are ephemeral (default 45s) and refreshed on interactive traffic. Anchoring only affects read-path (no change to write-through semantics).
2) Eviction smoothing: introduce token-weighted access counters with an exponential moving average (alpha tunable) and an eviction guard that disallows evicting an entry when recent access weight exceeds a threshold. Add a temporary grace window after anchor eviction to prevent immediate re-insert.
3) Queue merge + pacing: merge N per-tenant queues into a single sharded lane queue where each shard enforces per-session pacing tokens and a small fast-path lane for interactive p99-sensitive sessions. Replace three synchronization fences with a single compare-exchange rendezvous for lane acquisition.
4) Observability: add telemetry for anchor hits/misses, eviction decisions with why-cased labels (stale, low-weight, overcommit), queue-lane occupancy, and a trace tag to track session anchoring across request lifecycle.

Dependencies and Upgrades:
- Upgrade fmt to 10.1 to use the new formatting APIs in the anchor diagnostics log (PR linked).
- Bump libaio wrapper to 2.5 to stabilize mmap-backed snapshot writes used by kvcache compaction.
- Minor upgrade grpc to 1.52; ensure ABI compatibility in the async dispatch layer.

Deliverables:
- Library: libanchor (C++), eviction-smoother, merged-queue runtime module.
- Tests: unit tests for anchor lease refresh and grace window, integration test harness replaying a 72-hour production trace, and chaos tests that toggle anchors on/off during load ramps.
- Rollout plan: feature-flagged rollout to staging -> canary region (us-west-2) -> 25% region -> 100% region. Metrics gating: p99 token latency, kvcache miss rate, and error rate.

Observability & Runbook:
- Dashboards: anchor-hit/miss, eviction-reasons heatmap, per-lane occupancy, per-session pacing violations.
- Runbook steps: disable anchor flag, disable pacing bypass, or reduce anchor TTL. Revert path documented in PR.

Acceptance criteria:
- Staging replay benchmark shows <=10% regression at p95 and <=0% regression at p99 for baseline workloads; or improvement in kvcache miss storm frequency by >=60%.
- No increase in 5xx errors during canary.
- Code review approvals from infra and storage owners.

References:
- Design doc: https://redwood.atlassian.net/l/cp/ANCHOR-eviction-design
- Perf dashboard (staging trace): https://dash.redwood.ai/d/anchor/eviction-smoothing
- PR: https://github.com/redwood/inference/pull/12891
